text.en: A young seagull is afraid to fly, and a pilot is guided through a storm by a mysterious aeroplane. Two stories about flight.

In 'His First Flight' by Liam O'Flaherty, the young seagull is afraid to fly. His brothers and sister have already flown.
His parents and siblings call him and coax him, but he stays alone on the ledge, hungry and frightened.
His mother holds a piece of fish just out of his reach. Hunger pushes him to dive for it, and he finds himself flying.
The story shows how a small push can help us overcome fear, like a baby learning to walk.
In 'The Black Aeroplane' by Frederick Forsyth, the narrator flies an old Dakota over France to England at night, looking forward to breakfast at home.
He decides to risk flying through huge storm clouds. His compass and radio go dead and he is lost.
Then he sees another aeroplane, without lights, whose pilot waves, 'Follow me.' It leads him down to a runway just as his fuel runs out.
When he asks about the other pilot, the woman at the control centre says no other plane was flying; only his was on the radar.

problem.en: The Dakota had enough fuel for 10 more minutes and the pilot followed the plane for 30 minutes earlier. How long was the flight from the clouds to the runway, at least?

text.en: It is at least 40 minutes (after the storm began).

why.en: Use the story's figures only as practice.

requiredIdeas.en: The seagull is pushed by hunger
The pilot is helped by a mystery plane

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the pilot was not afraid

points.en: The seagull overcame fear to fly.
The pilot followed a black aeroplane to safety.
Both stories are about fear and courage.
The second story leaves a mystery.
